messages:
meera: quick sync — ran a fast pass of weight-only llm.int8 on aurora-13b for our summarization workload. latency down ~28%, tokens/sec up ~3.6x, but avg ROUGE-L dropped 2.1% on the longform slice. any ops/playbook notes for production rollout?
jon: did you use bitsandbytes' `llm.int8()` path or the huggingface BNB wrapper? tiny differences re: group-size and stable layernorm handling. also important: KV cache compat.
alex: numbers pls — batch size, seq len, CPU vs GPU mem, and whether you tipped any fallback to fp16 for long sequences.
meera: quick paste of config and results: 
```
model: aurora-13b
quant: llm.int8 (bitsandbytes)
batch: 4 (was 1 for latency p95)
seq: 1024
prefix-cache: enabled
throughput: 3.6x (median tokens/sec)
latency p95: -28%
rouge-L (longform slice): -2.1%
flags: --bnb-group-size 128 --bnb-use-llm-int8
```
meera: also attached eval artifact: s3://redwood-eval/1979991111/aurora13b-llmint8-longform-v1.json (ci-bot uploaded).
ci-bot: build 2026.03.18-aurora13b-llmint8 finished, artifacts -> https://ci.redwood.internal/1979991111 :white_check_mark:
jon: sanity checks: 1) verify tokenization parity (we had a case where byte-level vs new tokenizer produced shorter contexts for few-shot prompts) 2) run a small GPTQ/AWQ compare on the same slice — sometimes quality drop is quantizer-specific, not bitsandbytes per se.
sara: ops guidance suggestion: for any customer route that is sensitivity>0.8 (regression-risk), do a canary: 5% traffic -> monitor rouge/indicators for 24h, auto-fallback to fp16 if delta > 1.5% on the slice. Also set a per-route quantize-policy in routing: prefer llm.int8 for latency-first routes, prefer fp16 for fidelity-first.
alex: also watch cache eviction/clobbering. we saw higher repeated-token entropy when prefix cache entries were truncated at smaller group sizes. try bumping `--bnb-group-size` to 256 and re-eval.
meera: re-run scheduled with group-size=256 and batch 8. will post results.
jon: tiny note: for throughput accounting in console, make sure tokenizer-token counts used for billing match the eval metrics (we had mismatches counting whitespace tokens differently).
sara: reactive playbook snippet (for runbook): 
```
- run smoke on 1000 examples from each sensitive slice
- if rouge delta > 1.0% -> block rollout, notify ML-oncall
- if 0.5% < delta <= 1.0% -> canary 5% for 24h + increased sampling from failed examples
- else -> ramp to 50% over 6h
- auto-fallback: route -> fp16 after 24h of continuous regression
```
meera: thanks — posting results in ~2h. tagging @jon @alex for follow-ups. :eyes:
alex: :thumbsup:, also include GPU mem profiles (nvtop logs) — curious if transient OOMs were suppressed by caching and caused any silent retries.
meera: will include nvprof + nvtop snapshot. ci-bot: upload queued.
ci-bot: artifact upload complete -> s3://redwood-eval/1979991111/profiles.zip
jon: great — once we have the group-size=256 run we should add a short section to the model onboarding checklist: "preferred llm.int8 flags + fallback thresholds". small doc saves a lot of wake-up calls. :coffee:
